title: Vela: A Virtualized LLM Training System with GPU Direct RoCE
problem: LLM training at scale typically requires dedicated bare-metal GPU clusters with specialized interconnects (InfiniBand, NVLink), but deploying LLM training on cloud-native virtualized infrastructure using commodity hardware and standard Ethernet-based RDMA (RoCE) introduces performance challenges from virtualization overhead and suboptimal network stack interactions.
motivation: Making LLM training infrastructure accessible on commodity cloud hardware (RDMA over Converged Ethernet, KVM virtualization) broadens access and reduces cost, but achieving acceptable efficiency requires careful co-design of the virtualization and network layers.
method: Vela runs virtual machines (using KVM) where GPUs on different machines send data directly to each other (GPU Direct) without involving the host CPU. It uses SRIOV to give each virtual machine direct network access, and RoCE (a protocol that runs on standard Ethernet) for communication—avoiding specialized interconnects like InfiniBand. The team tested this on NVIDIA A100 GPUs in IBM Cloud with roughly 1500 machines, using model parallelism to train a 50-billion-parameter decoder-based language model. Insights from 2.5 years of production operation guided the design recommendations.
key_novelty: Vela shows that virtualized AI training with direct GPU communication and commodity Ethernet hardware achieves about 80% of bare-metal performance at 1500-GPU scale without specialized interconnects.
contributions: A production-scale cloud-native LLM training system architecture using KVM virtualization, SRIOV NICs, and GPU Direct RoCE.
~80% of ideal throughput training a 50B-parameter model at ~1500 GPU scale, and ~70% per-GPU FLOPS vs. single-VM HPL benchmark.
2.5 years of operational insights on designing, building, and operating virtualized AI infrastructure.
Identification of performance bottlenecks and improvement opportunities for future virtualized AI systems.

metrics.other: ~80% of ideal throughput at 1500-GPU scale (50B param model); ~70% per-GPU FLOPS vs single-VM HPL

limitations: The 80% efficiency figure leaves a 20% gap whose sources are acknowledged but not fully resolved in this work.
primary_theme: Cloud-native LLM training on virtualized GPU infrastructure with GPU Direct RoCE
